newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian police smash child pornography ring.
newsitem.headline: Austrian police smash child pornography ring.

text.p: Austrian police said on Tuesday they had smashed a child pornography ring in the northern province of Upper Austria and charged six men with abusing at least 19 boys over a seven-year period.
In a statement, Linz police said they had made the arrests between July 18 and August 5. They did not rule out extending the scope of their investigation.
"From the evidence we have obtained, we conclude that there are other unidentified victims in the locality," they said.
Police were alerted when the post office intercepted pornographic material from the United States addressed to one of the accused, a 51-year-old pensioner.
A search of the man's flat in the small town of Bad Goisern had yielded video evidence and a double mirror through which the young victims, aged five to 14, were filmed.
Police said the men, aged from 22 to 52, used threats and bribery to force the boys to cooperate. The accused also allegedly intimidated some parents who became suspicious.
The authorities urged local parents to be vigilant and to look out for signs that their children had extra pocket money.
